university: University of Science and Arts of Oklahoma
note: Thirty-five years in higher-education advancement -- Tulsa, OU-Tulsa, Rogers State, Friends University. CASE leadership is a higher-education association and does not count.

name: M. Wasiullah Khan
note: Teacher and administrator in the Pakistani education system, then an educational researcher and academic dean in the US before founding East-West University in 1980. Education throughout.

key: manuel martinez, ph.d.|dominican university new york
name: Manuel Martinez, Ph.D.
note: Eighteen years at Ohio Dominican rising from Spanish instructor to VP for academic affairs, then VPAA and dean of faculty at Mercy College of Ohio. One profile alludes to a business background but names no employer.

key: mayra charriez cordero|university of puerto rico at río piedras
name: Mayra Charriez Cordero
university: University of Puerto Rico at Río Piedras
note: Twenty-five years of administrative service inside the University of Puerto Rico -- dean of students, dean of education, VP for student affairs, continuing-education director, now interim rector.

name: Meggan Madden
note: Faculty and administrative posts at Arizona State, George Washington and the Middlebury Institute, then dean of academics at Principia. The CIES roles, the journal editorship and the UNESCO Chair are all academic.

name: Michael A. Thomas
note: Career is academic (Concordia Portland dean, then the Lutheran Institute for Theology and Culture), but he sits on the Orange County Business Council board -- a cross-sector regional business body, counted here the way chambers of commerce are.

name: Michael D. Hammond
note: Admissions and leadership-development roles at Taylor, a history professorship and department chairmanship at Southeastern, then provost at Taylor. Entirely within higher education.

key: michael e. steiper|suny at purchase college
name: Michael E. Steiper
note: Two decades at Hunter College as biological anthropologist and administrator, then provost at CUNY's College of Staten Island. Entirely within CUNY and SUNY.

name: Michael Ibba
note: An industrial post-doc at Novartis in Switzerland before the academic career (Copenhagen, then nineteen years at Ohio State, then Chapman). Counted the way other industrial research posts in this ledger are -- named corporate employment, professional rank.

name: Michael Lewis
note: Chemistry faculty at Saint Louis University from 2004, then associate provost, interim arts and sciences dean, and provost. A Harvard post-doc, no industry.

name: Michael I. Kotlikoff
note: Molecular physiologist: Penn veterinary faculty, then Cornell from 2000 -- biomedical sciences chair, vet dean, provost, and since 2025 president. No corporate or public board surfaced.

name: Michael M. Crow

ties.title: Co-founder; chairman of the board of trustees and director

ties.firm: National Advisory Council on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (U.S. Department of Commerce)
ties.title: Presidential appointee

note: Academic career throughout (Iowa State, Columbia, ASU), but he co-founded In-Q-Tel in 1999 and still chairs its board -- a venture-capital firm investing for the defence and intelligence communities, the most substantial standing corporate role in this stratum. His CV lists thirty boards; the education ones (Council for Aid to Education, Knight Commission) do not count, the business councils do.

name: Michael P. Godard
note: Exercise-science faculty then department chair, vice provost and interim provost at Central Missouri, provost at Southeast Missouri State. Twenty-five years entirely inside higher education.

name: Michael Rao
note: Four presidencies since 1992 (Mission College, Montana State-Northern, Central Michigan, VCU). His boards are all higher-education governance -- ACE chair, the NCAA, the Virginia Council of Presidents -- which do not count under this wave's rule.

name: Michael S. "Mike" Allen
note: Athletics director then VP for student affairs at Catholic University, and academic support roles at Florida Atlantic and UConn before that. Higher education throughout.

name: Michael S. Roth

ties.firm: Getty Research Institute (J. Paul Getty Trust)
ties.title: Associate Director; head of scholars and seminars programs

note: Between Scripps and the California College of the Arts he ran the scholars and seminars programs at the Getty Research Institute and served as its associate director -- a foundation post, counted the way other museum and cultural-institution roles are in this ledger.

name: Michael Sosulski
note: German studies at Kalamazoo, then provost at Wofford and president of Washington College. Entirely academic.

name: Michael T. Benson
note: A historian on his fifth presidency -- Snow, Southern Utah, Eastern Kentucky, Coastal Carolina, now WVU. No non-academic employer.

name: Michaele Whelan
note: Harvard, Tufts and Brandeis academic-affairs roles, then provost at Emerson. Entirely academic.

name: Michelle B. Larson
note: An astrophysicist who ran a major Chicago museum for twelve years -- president and CEO of the Adler Planetarium immediately before Clarkson -- plus a seat on NASA's federal science advisory committee.

name: Michelle Bligh
note: Organizational-behaviour professor at CGU from 2002, with a stint at NEOMA Business School. Her work with public and private organisations is faculty consulting in her own research area, which this wave does not count.

name: Michelle Johnston
note: Thirty years in higher education across four presidencies. The Secretary of Defense appointment to the Marine Corps University Board is a federal appointment but its substance is university governance, so it falls under the same rule as accreditation bodies and does not count.

name: Neil MacKinnon
note: Pharmacy academic: faculty, chair, centre director and dean across Dalhousie, Cincinnati and Arizona, then provost at Augusta. Twenty-six years entirely in higher education.

name: Nell Jessup Newton
note: Five law deanships (Hastings, Connecticut, Denver, Notre Dame, and interim at Miami and Wake Forest) and a federal Indian law treatise. Her ABA, AALS, LSAC and NALP roles are legal-education bodies, not private practice.

name: Nelson Edward Soto
note: IUPUI assistant dean, then curriculum and instruction leadership at Harrison College and provost at Union Institute. Harrison was a for-profit college, but the role was academic administration, so it reads as education-sector work rather than a corporate post.

name: Neville G. Pinto

ties.firm: Ohio Governor's Office of Workforce Transformation
ties.title: Board member

note: Forty years of chemical-engineering academia at Cincinnati and Louisville. The one non-academic tie is a seat on Ohio's Governor's Office of Workforce Transformation board -- state workforce policy, not higher-education governance, so it counts where the Inter-University Council of Ohio does not.

name: Nicole Farmer Hurd
note: Left a UVA deanship to run the national college-access nonprofit she founded, as CEO for roughly fifteen years before Lafayette. Counted as a nonprofit chief-executive role: the rule that excludes education work is about schools and governance boards, not about running an organisation.

name: Nicole S. Sampson
note: Chemical biologist: three decades at Stony Brook from assistant professor to arts and sciences dean, then dean and provost at Rochester.

name: Nicolle Cestero

ties.title: Staff role, member and public outreach

note: Career since 2011 is AIC administration -- chief of staff, COO, EVP, now president -- but it began at the Council on Foreign Relations in New York, a policy think tank rather than a school.

name: P. Barry Butler
note: Mechanical-engineering career entirely at Iowa before Embry-Riddle, but he sits on the boards of the Hoover Presidential Foundation and The Wings Club, the aviation industry society.

name: Pamela Whitten
note: Her own account has her working in corporate communications in Germany and then in health care in the United States before the doctorate -- clearly non-academic employment, but no employer is named in any source found, so this stays unknown rather than being guessed at. Her boards (AAU, Big Ten Council of Presidents) are higher-education bodies.

name: Patricia Draves
note: Chemistry faculty at Monmouth, then academic-affairs VP at Mount Union and president of Graceland. Entirely academic.

name: Patricia Ramsey
note: Biologist and academic administrator across Maryland, Virginia and North Carolina, then provost at Lincoln University. The year as a senior executive fellow at the Thurgood Marshall College Fund is an education-sector fellowship, and the MSCHE commissionership is accreditation -- neither counts.

name: Paul Alivisatos

ties.firm: Quantum Dot Corporation (acquired by Thermo Fisher)
ties.title: Founder

note: Nanoscience chemist who founded two companies out of his research -- Nanosys and Quantum Dot Corp, the latter now part of Thermo Fisher -- and sits on the CZ Biohub board. His Argonne and Fermi board chairmanships are ex officio as UChicago president and are not counted separately.

name: Patrick J. Wolfe
note: Academic career at Cambridge, Harvard, UCL and Purdue. The one outside seat is a trusteeship and non-executive directorship of the Alan Turing Institute, the UK's national data-science institute -- an independent charity rather than a university, so it counts.

name: Peggy Agouris
note: Remote-sensing and geoinformation scholar: department chair, science dean and research-centre director at George Mason, then provost at William & Mary.

name: Peter J. Mohler
note: Cardiovascular physiologist across Vanderbilt, Iowa and Ohio State, ending as EVP for research and chief scientific officer of the Wexner Medical Center -- an academic medical centre inside the university.

name: Peter Rodriguez
note: Economist whose career is otherwise academic (Texas A&M, Darden, dean of Rice Business), but he spent several years as an associate in JPMorgan Chase's Global Energy Group.

name: Penny L. Elkins
note: Began as a third-grade teacher and elementary administrator, then twenty-five years of Mercer faculty and senior administration. K-12 teaching is education-sector work and does not count.

key: paul r. taylor, o.s.b.|saint vincent college
name: Paul R. Taylor, O.S.B.
note: A Benedictine monk whose employment is all Saint Vincent, but who has advised the board of Straub Brewery since 2010 and sits on a hospital foundation and a historic-site board. CASE membership is higher education and does not count.

name: Paul Sniegowski
note: Twenty-seven years at Penn -- biology faculty from 1997, then dean of the College of Arts and Sciences. Entirely academic.

name: Peter Naccarato
note: Twenty years on the Marymount Manhattan English faculty, then academic-affairs VP and interim president. A food-studies scholar with no outside employer.

name: Phil Schubert
note: An accountant by training who audited at Arthur Andersen in Dallas before joining ACU in 1993, then rose through student financial services, CFO and EVP to the presidency.

name: Philip B. Oldham
note: A year as a Wellcome Research Fellow at Burroughs Wellcome between the doctorate and the Mississippi State faculty -- named pharmaceutical employment, counted like the other industrial research posts here.

name: Norman Hall
note: Student development, alumni affairs and advancement roles across Greenville, Azusa Pacific, Ashland, UC Santa Barbara and Southern Illinois. Entirely within higher education.

name: Noel E. Wilkin
note: Pharmacy-administration faculty at Ole Miss since 1996, then a decade in the provost's office. His national roles are pharmacy-education bodies.
